title: Establishment of Tzympe Castle
body: The Ottomans secure their first fortified stronghold on the European mainland at Tzympe, laying the groundwork for permanent expansion into Thrace.

title: Consolidation of the Gallipoli Foothold
body: Ottoman forces under Süleyman Pasha expand control around the Dardanelles straits following strategic local earthquakes that damaged Byzantine defenses.

title: Gallipoli seized
body: The Ottomans gain their first permanent European foothold on the Dardanelles.

title: Death of Stefan Dušan and Fragmentation of Serbia
body: The sudden death of Emperor Stefan Dušan removes the primary military obstacle to Ottoman expansion in the central Balkans, fracturing Serbian unity.

title: Expansion into Thrace
body: Ottoman raiding parties push further inland toward Çorlu and Lüleburgaz, isolating Constantinople from its Thracian hinterland.

title: Capture of Çorlu
body: Strategic regional centers in eastern Thrace are brought under direct Ottoman control, securing lines of communication across the straits.

title: Advance to the Maritsa River Valley
body: Ottoman forces probe deeper into western Thrace, establishing forward operating bases along the vital river trade routes.

title: First Investment of Adrianople
body: Ottoman armies initiate blockade operations around the major Thracian city of Adrianople (Edirne), signaling a shift from temporary raids to permanent conquest.

title: Accession of Murad I
body: Murad I succeeds Orhan, consolidating internal Anatolian control while accelerating systemic military expansion in Europe through the creation of the Janissary corps.

title: Capture of Didymoteicho
body: The key fortified center of Didymoteicho falls to Ottoman forces, tightening the noose around major Byzantine urban centers in Thrace.

title: Edirne becomes the European capital
body: Adrianople anchors Ottoman expansion into Thrace and the Balkans.

title: Battle of Dardanelles and Thracian Consolidation
body: Ottoman forces secure absolute dominance over regional supply lines connecting Anatolia to the newly established European capital at Edirne.

title: Campaigns in Western Thrace
body: Ottoman columns push toward the Rhodope Mountains and the Aegean coast, cutting off regional Christian principalities from one another.

title: Transfer of Court to Edirne
body: Edirne is officially designated as the primary imperial residence, symbolizing the shift of Ottoman strategic weight from Anatolia to the Balkans.

title: Amadeus VI's Crusade and Counter-Actions
body: Count Amadeus VI of Savoy temporarily recaptures Gallipoli for Byzantium, though Ottoman forces successfully maintain their core positions in Thrace.

title: Securing the Maritsa Corridor
body: Ottoman armies systematically pacify the towns along the Maritsa valley, ensuring unobstructed movement toward the central Balkans.

title: Reduction of Local Bulgarian Strongholds
body: Border fortresses in southern Bulgaria are brought under tributary status following coordinated pressure from Edirne.

title: Capture of Plovdiv (Philippopolis)
body: The major Thracian city of Plovdiv falls to Ottoman arms, opening the direct approach to the Sofia valley and the interior Balkans.

title: Diplomatic and Military Pressure on Byzantium
body: Emperor John V Palaiologos is forced to accept tributary status and acknowledge Ottoman military supremacy in Europe.

title: Battle of Maritsa
body: An Ottoman force decisively routs a much larger allied Serbian and Bulgarian army at the Maritsa River, establishing unchallenged hegemony over Macedonia.

title: Subjugation of Macedonia
body: Following the Maritsa disaster, local lords in northern Greece and Macedonia accept Ottoman suzerainty and pay regular tribute.

title: Byzantine-Ottoman Joint Campaign in Anatolia
body: Emperor John V is compelled to march alongside Murad I to suppress rebellious Ottoman princes in Anatolia, marking deep vassalage.

title: Encroachment on Northern Bulgaria
body: Ottoman raiding columns reach the northern slopes of the Balkan mountains, pressuring local Tsardom of Tarnovo outposts.

title: Acquisition of Germiyan and Hamid territories
body: Diplomatic marriages and strategic land purchases in Anatolia peacefully integrate key central principalities into the Ottoman sphere.

title: Byzantine Civil War Intervention
body: Murad I backs Andronikos IV Palaiologos in a Byzantine civil war, securing the retrocession of Gallipoli to Ottoman control.

title: Consolidation of Aegean Thrace
body: Coastal fortresses along the northern Aegean are systematically integrated into the expanding provincial administrative network.

title: War with the Karamanids
body: Rising tensions in central Anatolia lead to open conflict with the powerful Karamanid Beylik over regional hegemony.

title: Restoration of Manuel II and Balkan Garrisoning
body: Ottoman forces manage shifting Byzantine alliances while strengthening permanent garrisons across Rumelia.

title: Campaigns in Macedonia and Albania
body: Ottoman commanders push westward toward the Adriatic watershed, subduing local warlords in western Macedonia and northern Albania.

title: Annexation of Tekke Lands
body: The coastal Anatolian principality of Tekke is purchased, expanding Ottoman control toward the Mediterranean ports.

title: Capture of Sofia
body: Strategic fortress city of Sofia falls to Ottoman forces, cutting the vital connection between Serbia and Bulgaria.

title: First Siege of Thessaloniki
body: Ottoman forces under Lala Şahin Pasha begin the long-term blockade and investment of the major Byzantine port of Thessaloniki.

title: Skirmishing in Northern Greece
body: Ottoman raiders penetrate deep into Thessaly and Epirus, destabilizing local independent Christian rulers.

title: Capture of Niš
body: The vital fortress city of Niš falls to Murad I, breaking Moravian-Serbian defensive lines and opening the path to Kosovo.

title: Subjugation of the Karamanids
body: Murad I inflicts a major defeat on the Karamanids at Konya, enforcing temporary submission across central Anatolia.

title: Fall of Thessaloniki
body: The prolonged Ottoman siege culminates in the surrender of Thessaloniki, extending direct imperial control across coastal Macedonia.

title: Battle of Bileća
body: An Ottoman expeditionary force in Bosnia experiences a rare tactical check against local Bosnian and Zeta coalition forces.

title: Battle of Kosovo
body: Serbian power is broken after a costly battle; Ottoman influence deepens in the central Balkans, and Murad I is assassinated.

title: Bayezid's Rapid Anatolian Consolidation
body: Newly enthroned Bayezid I swiftly campaigns across western Anatolia, annexing Aydınoğlu, Saruhanoğlu, and Menteşe to secure the rear before European operations.

title: First Blockade of Constantinople
body: Bayezid I initiates land blockades around Constantinople and campaigns along the lower Danube to secure northern borders.

title: Annexation of Kastamonu and Amasya
body: Bayezid eliminates the Candaroglu power in northern Anatolia, extending Ottoman borders to the Black Sea coast.

title: Fall of Tarnovo and Subjugation of Bulgaria
body: Ottoman forces capture the Bulgarian capital of Tarnovo, ending the Bulgarian Tsardom and converting it directly into an Ottoman province.

title: Establishment of the Blockade Ring (Anadolu Hisarı)
body: Bayezid builds Anadolu Hisarı on the Bosporus to tighten the permanent strangulation of Constantinople.

title: Battle of Rovine
body: Bayezid invades Wallachia; despite heavy fighting, Prince Mircea the Elder maintains local autonomy while acknowledging Ottoman tributary terms.

title: Battle of Nicopolis
body: A crusading army is defeated, confirming Ottoman control over Bulgaria.

title: War with Karamanid Beylik
body: Bayezid decisively defeats the Karamanids at the Battle of Akçay, executing the ruler Ali Bey and absorbing central Anatolian territories.

title: Expedition to Eastern Anatolia
body: Ottoman forces push toward Sivas and Malatya, clashing with local Turkmen states and brushing against Mamluk spheres of influence.

title: Capture of Dulkadir Outposts
body: Bayezid consolidates gains in eastern Anatolia, creating friction with Timur as the two expanding empires share a common border.

title: Timur Sacks Sivas
body: Timur captures and destroys the Ottoman garrison at Sivas, signaling the impending existential clash between the Ottomans and Timurids.

title: Preparations for the Great Clash
body: Both Bayezid I and Timur mobilize massive armies across Anatolia, setting the stage for the decisive showdown.

title: Battle of Ankara & Collapse
body: Timur crushes Bayezid I. The first Anatolian unification fractures as old beyliks re-assert independence during the Ottoman Interregnum.

title: Beginning of the Ottoman Interregnum
body: Bayezid's sons (Süleyman, İsa, Mehmed, and Musa) begin a bitter decade-long civil war for control of the fractured remnants of the state.

title: Interregnum: Power Struggles in Rumelia
body: Süleyman Çelebi consolidates control over Ottoman European territories while Anatolian brothers fight for regional supremacy.

title: Interregnum: Mehmed Çelebi in Amasya
body: Mehmed Çelebi builds a strong power base in central Anatolia, organizing resources to challenge his rivals.

title: Interregnum: Conflict between Süleyman and Musa
body: Brothers clash for dominance over European and northwestern Anatolian territories.

title: Interregnum: Shift in Regional Alliances
body: Byzantine and Balkan rulers exploit the Ottoman civil war by playing rival princes against one another.

title: Interregnum: Musa Çelebi's Campaign in Rumelia
body: Musa crosses into Europe with support from Wallachia, challenging Süleyman Çelebi's dominance in the Balkans.

title: Interregnum: Fall of Süleyman Çelebi
body: Musa Çelebi defeats Süleyman Çelebi, taking control of the European territories and briefly reunifying Rumelia.

title: Interregnum: Clashes between Musa and Mehmed
body: Mehmed Çelebi allies with Byzantine Emperor Manuel II to cross the Bosporus and contest Musa's rule in Europe.

title: Interregnum: Siege of Constantinople by Musa
body: Musa Çelebi besieges Constantinople in retaliation for Byzantine support of Mehmed Çelebi.

title: Interregnum: Escalation in Rumelia
body: Mehmed Çelebi and Serbian allies wage intense campaigns against Musa's forces in the western Balkans.

title: Battle of Çamurlu & End of Interregnum
body: Mehmed I defeats Musa Çelebi with Serbian backing, reunifying the Ottoman state and ending the destructive 11-year civil war.

title: Mehmed I Campaigns in Anatolia
body: The newly reunited state asserts its authority over rebellious western Anatolian principalities, restoring pre-Ankara borders.

title: First Naval Clash with Venice
body: The emerging Ottoman navy fights its first major engagement against the Venetian fleet off Gallipoli, highlighting rising maritime competition.

title: Bedreddin Revolt
body: A major social and religious rebellion led by Sheikh Bedreddin across Rumelia and western Anatolia is successfully suppressed by Mehmed I.

title: Campaigns in Wallachia
body: Ottoman punitive expeditions cross the Danube to enforce tribute collection from Wallachian princes.

title: Capture of Samsun
body: Mehmed I incorporates Samsun and surrounding Black Sea coastal ports into the Ottoman domain, securing regional trade.

title: Consolidation of Black Sea Trade
body: Ottoman naval and commercial presence expands along the southern Black Sea littoral.

title: Suppression of Anatolian Dissidents
body: Final mopping-up operations against lingering pretenders and rebellious local lords in Anatolia.

title: Accession of Murad II and Pretender Revolts
body: Mehmed I dies; his son Murad II ascends the throne and immediately faces a Byzantine-backed pretender revolt (Düzmece Mustafa).

title: Start of the Siege of Thessalonica
body: In retaliation for the Byzantine Empire releasing and backing the pretender Mustafa Çelebi, Sultan Murad II defeated the rival claimant and launched an immediate blockade and siege against Thessalonica.

title: First Ottoman invasion of the Morea
body: Large-scale raid initiating Ottoman interest in the Peloponnese region.

title: Treaty with Byzantium and Venice
body: Murad II concludes favorable peace treaties, stabilizing European borders and confirming annual Byzantine tribute.

title: Anatolian Campaign against Menteşe and Aydın
body: Murad II annexes remaining western Anatolian principalities, solidifying central imperial control over Asia Minor.

title: Annexation of Hamid
body: The territories of the Hamid principality are formally incorporated into the Ottoman administrative structure.

title: Acquisition of Golubac
body: The strategic Danubian fortress of Golubac is secured following the death of Despot Stefan Lazarević of Serbia.

title: Campaigns in the Morava Valley
body: Ottoman forces clash with Hungarian border armies for control of key transit routes into central Europe.

title: Siege of Thessalonica Intensifies
body: Blockade operations around Thessalonica tighten as Venetian resistance wanes.

title: Fall of Thessalonica to Murad II
body: Murad II captures Thessalonica from the Venetians, securing a major Aegean port and dealing a severe blow to Venetian commercial networks.

title: Campaigns in Albania
body: Ottoman armies launch extensive campaigns into central and southern Albania to establish direct administrative control.

title: First Timar Survey in Albania
body: Comprehensive land and revenue surveys (tahrir) are initiated in newly conquered Albanian territories to integrate them into the Ottoman military-feudal system.

title: Expeditions into Serbia
body: Ottoman forces conduct punitive raids into Serbian territory to enforce vassal compliance.

title: Clashes with John Hunyadi's Precursors
body: Hungarian commanders begin organizing defensive leagues along the southern border, marking the rise of John Hunyadi.

title: Border Skirmishes in Transylvania
body: Low-intensity warfare characterizes the mountainous borders between Ottoman vassal states and the Hungarian Kingdom.

title: Rebellion in Albania
body: Early local uprisings break out against Ottoman land registration and timar distribution in mountainous Albanian districts.

title: Death of Sigismund and Hungarian Instability
body: The death of Holy Roman Emperor and Hungarian King Sigismund plunges central Europe into political instability, prompting Ottoman opportunistic raids.

title: Invasion of Transylvania
body: Murad II leads a massive expedition into Transylvania, sacking towns and capturing significant loot and prisoners.

title: Fall of Smederevo
body: Ottoman forces capture the mighty Serbian fortress of Smederevo, effectively extinguishing the independent Serbian Despotate for the first time.

title: Siege of Belgrade
body: Murad II lays siege to the crucial frontier fortress of Belgrade, but stubborn Hungarian defense repels the Ottoman assault.

title: John Hunyadi's Counter-Raids
body: John Hunyadi inflicts several defeats on regional Ottoman commanders in Transylvania and Wallachia, boosting Christian morale.

title: Battles of the Iron Gates
body: Hunyadi successfully repels Ottoman punitive armies in Transylvania and Wallachia, checking the Ottoman advance.

title: Skanderbeg Rebellion begins
body: Gjergj Kastrioti (Skanderbeg) seizes Krujë and defects, launching a 25-year war of liberation that opens a deep pocket in western Rumelia.

title: Varna
body: The crusade of Varna is destroyed on the Black Sea coast.

title: Crusader Operations on the Danube
body: Naval and land crusader forces attempt minor operations along the lower Danube following Varna, with limited strategic impact.

title: Siege of the Hexamilion Wall
body: Ottoman forces under Murad II break through the defensive wall at the Isthmus of Corinth, devastating the Peloponnese.

title: Venetian-Ottoman Treaty
body: Venice and the Ottoman Empire conclude a trade and peace agreement, isolating Skanderbeg's resistance in Albania.

title: Second Battle of Kosovo
body: Murad II crushes John Hunyadi's invading army in a three-day battle at Kosovo Polje, permanently ending Hungarian hopes of expelling Ottomans from Europe.

title: Border Stabilization
body: Quiet period on the European frontier as Murad II consolidates administrative control following Kosovo.

title: First Siege of Krujë
body: Murad II personally leads an army to besiege Skanderbeg's stronghold at Krujë, but fails to capture it due to fierce resistance and harsh winter conditions.

title: Accession of Mehmed II
body: Mehmed II ascends the throne for his second reign, immediately beginning meticulous preparations for the final conquest of Constantinople.

title: Construction of Boğazkesen (Rumeli Hisarı)
body: Mehmed II builds the massive fortress of Rumeli Hisarı on the European shore of the Bosporus, completely cutting off Constantinople from Black Sea relief.

title: Constantinople falls
body: Mehmed II captures the Byzantine capital and turns Istanbul into the imperial center.

title: First Campaign in Serbia
body: Mehmed II invades Serbia, forcing Despot Đurađ Branković to pay increased tribute and submit to Ottoman terms.

title: Conquest of Novo Brdo
body: Ottoman forces capture the rich silver-mining center of Novo Brdo in Kosovo, boosting imperial revenues.

title: Siege of Belgrade
body: Mehmed II is wounded and repulsed at the Siege of Belgrade by John Hunyadi and John Capistran, halting Ottoman expansion into Hungary for decades.

title: Skanderbeg's Victory at Albulena
body: Skanderbeg inflicts a heavy defeat on an Ottoman expeditionary force at Albulena in Albania.

title: Conquest of northern Morea
body: Ottoman advance forces the Despotate of ghosts and local lords into tributary status in the Peloponnese.

title: Annexation of the Serbian Despotate
body: The fortress of Smederevo is peacefully surrendered or captured, ending the final remnants of the medieval Serbian state.

title: Conquest of the Despotate of the Morea
body: Final annexation of the Peloponnese, ending the Despotate and extinguishing Byzantine rule in mainland Greece.

title: Conquest of Trebizond and Amasra
body: Mehmed II eliminates the Empire of Trebizond and Genoese Amasra, bringing the southern Black Sea coast entirely under Ottoman control.

title: Campaign against Vlad III Dracula
body: Mehmed II launches the famous campaign into Wallachia, encountering the psychological warfare of the Night Attack and replacing Dracula with Radu cel Frumos.

title: Conquest of Bosnia and Outbreak of Ottoman-Venetian War
body: Mehmed II rapidly conquers the Kingdom of Bosnia, executing King Stephen Tomašević, while a long 16-year war breaks out with Venice over Aegean outposts.

title: Jajce Campaign
body: Mehmed II attempts to recapture Jajce in Bosnia from Hungarian forces but is forced to lift the siege.

title: Skirmishing in Venetian Albania
body: Protracted border warfare against Venetian coastal enclaves and Skanderbeg's forces in the western Balkans.

title: Mehmed II's Campaign in Albania
body: Mehmed II personally leads a large army into Albania to crush Skanderbeg's resistance and besiege Krujë once again, without decisive subjugation.

title: Death of Skanderbeg's Resistance Strains
body: Despite ongoing guerrilla warfare, Skanderbeg maintains independence shortly before his death in 1468.

title: Annexation of Karamanid Territories
body: Mehmed II exploits internal divisions in the Karamanid Beylik to annex Konya and central Anatolian heartlands.

title: Venetian Raids on Aegean Coast
body: Venetian fleets launch disruptive raids along the western Anatolian coast, sacking towns like İzmir.

title: Conquest of Negroponte (Euboea)
body: Mehmed II constructs a pontoon bridge to capture the heavily fortified Venetian naval base of Negroponte, stunning European powers.

title: Fortification of the Danube Frontier
body: Ottoman engineers construct new fortresses along the Danube to counter Hungarian river patrols.

title: Aq Qoyunlu Invasions in Anatolia
body: Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu confederation invades eastern Anatolia with Western encouragement.

title: Battle of Otlukbeli
body: Mehmed II uses modern artillery to defeat Uzun Hasan, extending absolute hegemony deep into the eastern Anatolian highlands.

title: Siege of Shkodra
body: Ottoman forces besiege the Venetian-held Albanian fortress of Shkodra, facing stiff resistance.

title: Crimea enters Ottoman orbit & Battle of Vaslui
body: Genoese Black Sea ports fall and the Crimean Khanate becomes an Ottoman vassal, though Stephen the Great crushes an Ottoman army at Vaslui in Moldavia.

title: Campaign of Valea Albă
body: Mehmed II personally invades Moldavia, defeating Stephen the Great at Valea Albă, though unable to secure permanent subjugation.

title: Venetian Peace Feelers
body: Exhausted by a 15-year war, Venice and the Ottoman Empire begin serious diplomatic exchanges.

title: Renewed Siege of Shkodra
body: Ottoman armies renew assaults on Shkodra until the Venetian peace treaty forces its ceding.

title: Albania fully conquered & Treaty of Constantinople
body: Following the fall of Shkodër and the Treaty of Constantinople, Venetian-held outposts are ceded, incorporating Albania completely into Rumelia.

title: Otranto Landing and Siege of Rhodes
body: Ottoman forces land at Otranto in southern Italy while simultaneously launching a failed siege of the Knights Hospitaller at Rhodes.
largest_rival: Kingdom of Naples and Knights Hospitaller

title: Death of Mehmed II and Civil War
body: Mehmed II dies during preparations for a new campaign; a succession struggle erupts between his sons Bayezid II and Cem Sultan.

title: Sack of Kyiv by Crimean Allies
body: Crimean Tatars acting under Ottoman-aligned orbits sack Kyiv, while Cem Sultan flees to European protection after losing the civil war.

title: Consolidation of Bayezid II's Rule
body: Bayezid II stabilizes domestic administration and secures the western frontiers after the dynastic disruption.

title: Kilia and Akkerman taken
body: Moldavia loses its Black Sea outlets and accepts Ottoman suzerainty under Bayezid II.

title: Outbreak of Ottoman-Mamluk War
body: Border disputes in Cilicia spark a protracted, inconclusive war between the Ottoman Empire and the Mamluk Sultanate.

title: Frontier Clashes in Cilicia
body: Ottoman and Mamluk armies trade border fortresses in southern Anatolia with no decisive winner.

title: Crimean Successes on the Northern Steppe
body: Crimean Tatar raids secure dominance across the Pontic-Caspian steppe, feeding slaves and tribute into the Ottoman economic sphere.

title: Battle of Ağaççayırı
body: Mamluk forces inflict a heavy defeat on the Ottoman army in Cilicia, highlighting logistical strains on the southern front.

title: Cem Sultan Handed to the Papacy
body: Exile Cem Sultan is transferred to Pope Innocent VIII, becoming a useful diplomatic hostage against Bayezid II's European ambitions.

title: Stalemate with Mamluks
body: Weary of inconclusive warfare, the Ottomans and Mamluks negotiate a tentative cessation of hostilities in Cilicia.

title: Treaty with Mamluks & Ryazan Raids
body: A peace treaty with the Mamluks restores pre-war borders, while Crimean Tatars raid deep into Muscovite Ryazan.

title: Expulsion of Sephardic Jews
body: Bayezid II famously dispatches the Ottoman navy to rescue Sephardic Jews expelled from Spain, welcoming them into major imperial cities.

title: Battle of Krbava Field
body: Ottoman irregular cavalry (Akıncıs) inflict a catastrophic defeat on Croatian nobility in a devastating raid.

title: Italian War Disruptions
body: The French invasion of Italy under Charles VIII shifts European focus away from the Ottoman frontier.

title: Death of Cem Sultan
body: Cem Sultan dies in Naples, removing a major source of European leverage and internal dynastic anxiety for Bayezid II.

title: Montenegro Campaigns
body: Ottoman forces tighten control over the mountainous terrain of Zeta and Montenegro.

title: Polish-Ottoman Border Clashes
body: Tensions flare along the Moldavian frontier as Polish armies attempt to intervene in Danubian affairs.

title: Raid into Poland
body: Crimean Tatars and Ottoman auxiliary forces launch a massive punitive raid deep into Polish territory.

title: Outbreak of Ottoman-Venetian War
body: Bayezid II launches a major naval and land war against Venice, capturing Lepanto and dominating the Ionian Sea.

title: Fall of Modon and Coron
body: The Ottoman navy under Kemal Reis defeats Venice at the Battle of Zonchio, followed by the capture of key Venetian naval stations at Modon and Coron.

title: Rise of the Safavid Empire
body: Shah Ismail I founds the Safavid dynasty in Persia, establishing a militant Shia state that will become the primary existential rival to the Ottomans.

title: Peace with Venice
body: Venice cedes its remaining major Greek mainland strongholds to the Ottoman Empire, concluding the naval conflict.

title: Treaty with Poland
body: Poland signs a peace treaty recognizing Ottoman hegemony over Moldavian ports and border regions.

title: Internal Safavid Expansion
body: Shah Ismail consolidates control over western Iran, absorbing territories that border Ottoman eastern provinces.

title: Great Earthquake in Istanbul
body: A massive earthquake (known as the Lesser Judgement Day) heavily damages Istanbul, prompting widespread imperial reconstruction.

title: Qizilbash Propaganda in Anatolia
body: Safavid agents (Qizilbash) actively spread Shia militant propaganda among discontented Turkmen tribes in eastern and central Anatolia.

title: Safavid Raids through Anatolia
body: Shah Ismail's forces march through Ottoman-claimed territory to attack Dulkadir, alarming the Sublime Porte.

title: Safavid Capture of Baghdad
body: Shah Ismail conquers Baghdad, bringing Safavid power directly to the borders of Ottoman Mesopotamia.

title: Şahkulu Rebellion
body: A massive pro-Safavid Qizilbash uprising breaks out in Anatolia, threatening Bursa before being brutally suppressed by Ottoman forces.

title: Succession Crisis Looms
body: Aging Bayezid II faces intense factional struggle among his sons (Ahmed, Korkud, and Selim) over the imperial succession.

title: Selim's Coup and Abdication of Bayezid II
body: Prince Selim mobilizes Janissary support, forces the abdication of his father Bayezid II, and ascends the throne as Selim I.

title: Purge of Domestic Rivals
body: Selim I eliminates his brothers Ahmed and Korkud to secure undivided control over the empire, turning his full attention east.

title: Massacre of Qizilbash Sympathizers
body: Selim I orders a comprehensive census and purge of pro-Safavid Shia sympathizers in Anatolia to secure his rear.

title: Battle of Chaldiran
body: Selim I crushes Shah Ismail's Qizilbash army using superior artillery and firearms, annexing northern Iraq and eastern Anatolia.

title: Political Unification of Anatolia
body: Following victory at Turnadağ, the last major independent Anatolian beylik is formally eliminated, bringing Asia Minor under total Ottoman administration.

title: Battle of Marj Dabiq & Capture of Algiers
body: Selim I destroys the Mamluk army in Syria, opening the path to Egypt, while Ottoman corsairs establish a foothold in Algiers.

title: Conquest of Egypt and Caliphate Transfer
body: Selim I defeats the Mamluks at Ridaniyye, capturing Cairo and ending the Mamluk Sultanate; the Caliphate is traditionally transferred to the Ottoman house.

title: Integration of Levantine and Egyptian Provinces
body: Selim I organizes new administrative provinces in Syria and Egypt, securing vast trade networks linking the Red Sea to the Mediterranean.

title: Barbarossa Swears Fealty
body: Hayreddin Barbarossa places Algiers under Ottoman protection, laying the foundation for North African maritime eyalets.

title: Accession of Suleiman the Magnificent
body: Selim I dies; his son Suleiman I (the Magnificent) ascends the throne, ushering in the golden age of Ottoman military and cultural expansion.

title: Belgrade falls & Great Crimean Raid
body: Suleiman opens the road into Hungary by capturing Belgrade, while Crimean forces launch a massive raid reaching the outskirts of Moscow.

title: Conquest of Rhodes
body: Suleiman leads a massive amphibious siege to expel the Knights Hospitaller from Rhodes, securing secure sea lanes to Egypt.

title: Appointment of Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha
body: Ibrahim Pasha is elevated to Grand Vizier, beginning a long period of centralized bureaucratic and military reform.

title: Rebellion of Ahmed Pasha in Egypt
body: A rogue governor's revolt in Egypt is swiftly crushed, leading to administrative reorganization by Ibrahim Pasha.

title: Preparations for Hungarian Campaign
body: Suleiman masses imperial forces for a decisive strike against the Kingdom of Hungary.

title: Battle of Mohacs
body: The medieval Kingdom of Hungary collapses after a catastrophic defeat and King Louis II's death.

title: Habsburg-Ottoman Contest for Hungary
body: Ferdinand of Habsburg claims the Hungarian crown, sparking a prolonged struggle with Ottoman-backed John Zápolya.

title: Expedition to Secure Buda
body: Ottoman armies sweep back into Hungary to reinstate John Zápolya against Habsburg incursions.

title: First Siege of Vienna & Capture of Peñón of Algiers
body: Suleiman leads the grand army to the walls of Vienna but fails to capture it due to harsh weather and logistics, while Hayreddin Barbarossa takes the Spanish fortress in Algiers.

title: Stalemate in Hungary
body: Ferdinand's counter-siege of Buda fails, cementing a fractured territorial division in Central Europe.

title: Fortification of Frontiers
body: Both the Ottomans and Habsburgs construct extensive border fortresses along the disputed Hungarian corridor.

title: Campaign of Güns (Kőszeg)
body: Suleiman leads another massive army into Hungary, bogged down by the minor fortress of Kőszeg, preventing a second major push on Vienna.

title: Treaty of Constantinople with Habsburgs
body: Ferdinand and Suleiman sign a landmark treaty recognizing Ottoman suzerainty over central Hungary and treating Ferdinand as an equal to the Grand Vizier.

title: Capture of Baghdad & Temporary Tunis Occupation
body: Suleiman launches the Two Iraqs campaign, capturing Baghdad from the Safavids, while Barbarossa temporarily seizes Tunis.

title: Spanish Reconquest of Tunis
body: Emperor Charles V leads a massive Christian fleet to capture Tunis from Barbarossa, temporarily restoring Spanish influence in North Africa.

title: Franco-Ottoman Alliance & Execution of Ibrahim Pasha
body: Suleiman concludes the historic Franco-Ottoman alliance with Francis I against the Habsburgs and orders the execution of Grand Vizier Ibrahim Pasha.

title: Campaign of Corfu and Venetian War
body: Suleiman launches an invasion of Venetian-held Corfu and the Italian coast, sparking a new maritime war with Venice.

title: Battle of Preveza & Moldovan Campaign
body: Hayreddin Barbarossa crushes the Holy League fleet at Preveza, securing Ottoman naval supremacy in the Mediterranean, while Suleiman subdues Moldavia.

title: Siege of Castelnuovo
body: Ottoman forces recapture Castelnuovo (Herceg Novi) from Spanish troops after a brutal siege.

title: Venetian Peace Treaty
body: Venice cedes its remaining Aegean and Peloponnesian possessions to the Ottomans and pays a heavy indemnity.

title: Budin Eyalet established
body: Central Hungary becomes directly administered Ottoman territory (Budin Eyalet) while Transylvania becomes a vassal buffer following John Zápolya's death.

title: Habsburg Siege of Buda Repulsed
body: Ferdinand's massive attempt to recapture Buda is comprehensively smashed by Ottoman relief armies.

title: Campaign of Esztergom
body: Suleiman leads a successful campaign in Hungary, capturing Esztergom, Székesfehérvár, and Siklós.

title: Truce with Habsburgs
body: Exhausted by continuous campaigning, Suleiman and Charles V agree to a temporary truce in Hungary.

title: Renewal of Truce
body: Diplomatic efforts maintain peace along the central European borderlands.

title: Death of Hayreddin Barbarossa
body: Legendary grand admiral Hayreddin Barbarossa passes away, leaving a dominant Ottoman naval legacy managed by successors like Turgut Reis.

title: Five-Year Truce Signed
body: Ferdinand and Charles V formally sign a five-year truce with the Ottoman Empire, agreeing to pay annual tribute for Habsburg lands in Hungary.

title: Third Campaign of Tabriz
body: Suleiman launches his second major expedition against Safavid Persia, occupying Tabriz and advancing through Armenia.

title: Operations in the Georgian Valleys
body: Ottoman armies secure border districts in southern Georgia during the Persian campaign.

title: Construction of Süleymaniye Mosque
body: Master architect Mimar Sinan begins construction of the iconic Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul, defining classical Ottoman architecture.

title: Capture of Tripoli
body: Turgut Reis and Sinan Pasha capture Tripoli from the Knights of St. John, expanding Ottoman North African dominance.

title: Temesvar Eyalet created & Siege of Eger
body: The Banat frontier is reorganized as the Temesvar Eyalet, though the Ottoman siege of Eger in northern Hungary fails.

title: Invasion of Corsica & Execution of Şehzade Mustafa
body: A joint Franco-Ottoman fleet invades Corsica, while Suleiman orders the execution of his eldest son Şehzade Mustafa over succession intrigues.

title: Nakhchivan Campaign
body: Ottoman devastation of Safavid territory leading to peace negotiations.

title: Treaty of Amasya
body: First formal Ottoman–Safavid peace treaty; Iraq and eastern Anatolia are recognized as permanently Ottoman.

title: Siege of Szigetvár Prep
body: Local skirmishing and fortification dominate the Hungarian border as regional commanders vie for advantage.

title: Completion of Süleymaniye Mosque
body: The grand Süleymaniye complex is inaugurated in Istanbul, symbolizing the cultural height of Suleiman's reign.

title: Naval Engagement at Djerba Prep
body: Turgut Reis expands Ottoman naval dominance across the western Mediterranean basin.

title: Battle of Konya (Civil War)
body: Suleiman's surviving sons Bayezid and Selim clash in a civil war over succession; Bayezid is defeated and flees to Persia.

title: Battle of Djerba
body: Ottoman fleet under Piyale Pasha and Turgut Reis utterly destroys a Christian coalition fleet off the island of Djerba.

title: Execution of Şehzade Bayezid
body: Following diplomatic agreements with Shah Ismail, fugitive Prince Bayezid and his sons are executed in Safavid territory, securing Selim as sole heir.

title: Extension of Habsburg Truce
body: Suleiman signs an eight-year peace extension with Ferdinand I, stabilizing the European frontier.

title: Border Skirmishes in Hungary
body: Minor local infractions occur along the fortified border zones despite official truces.

title: St. Elmo Preparations (Malta Prep)
body: Intelligence reports gather in Istanbul regarding the Knights Hospitaller buildup on Malta.

title: Great Siege of Malta
body: Ottoman forces under Mustafa Pasha and Piyale Pasha attempt to dislodge the Knights Hospitaller from Malta but suffer a famous, bloody defeat.

title: Szigetvár and Suleiman's death
body: Suleiman dies in his tent during the capture of Szigetvár; Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha successfully conceals his death to maintain army morale.

title: Accession Consolidation under Sokollu
body: Capable Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha effectively runs the empire under easygoing Sultan Selim II, initiating ambitious infrastructure projects like the Suez canal proposals.

title: Treaty of Adrianople with Habsburgs
body: Sokollu signs a landmark peace treaty with Maximilian II, ending hostilities in Hungary and recognizing mutual spheres of influence.

title: Astrakhan Expedition
body: An ambitious Ottoman-Crimean expedition to capture Astrakhan and cut off Russian expansion fails due to logistical collapse and harsh winter.

title: Invasion of Cyprus
body: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha initiates the conquest of Venetian Cyprus, capturing Nicosia and blockading Famagusta.

title: Lepanto, Fall of Cyprus & Burning of Moscow
body: Cyprus is fully conquered after the fall of Famagusta, but the Ottoman fleet suffers a catastrophic defeat at Lepanto against the Holy League, while Devlet I Giray burns Moscow.

title: Rapid Fleet Reconstruction
body: In an astonishing industrial feat, Sokollu Mehmed Pasha rebuilds the entire Ottoman navy within six winter months, deterring Holy League follow-up attacks.

title: Treaty with Venice
body: Venice signs a separate peace treaty ceding Cyprus to the Ottoman Empire and paying a massive war indemnity.

title: Ottoman Reconquest of Tunis
body: Kılıç Ali Pasha leads an expedition to permanently annex Tunisia from Spanish control, ending the local Hafsid dynasty.

title: Accession of Murad III
body: Selim II dies; Murad III ascends the throne, continuing the vizierate of Sokollu Mehmed Pasha amidst rising court factionalism.

title: Safavid Succession Crisis Exploited
body: The death of Shah Tahmasp I triggers chaos in Persia, prompting the Ottoman war party to push for a resumption of hostilities in the east.

title: Outbreak of Ottoman-Safavid War (1578–1590)
body: Lala Mustafa Pasha leads an Ottoman invasion into the Caucasus, sparking a long and economically draining war with Persia.

title: Battle of the Swords (Çıldır)
body: Ottoman forces defeat Safavid armies in Georgia, establishing forward military bases in Tiflis and Shirvan.

title: Assassination of Sokollu Mehmed Pasha
body: The powerful Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha is assassinated by a dervish, removing the last steady hand of the classic era and accelerating court corruption.

title: Anglo-Ottoman Trade Capitulations
body: Queen Elizabeth I secures trade privileges (capitulations) for English merchants in the Ottoman Empire, countering Spanish hegemony.

title: Caucasian Campaigns Continue
body: Özdemiroğlu Osman Pasha campaigns extensively across Dagestan and Shirvan to secure mountain passes against Safavid counter-attacks.

title: Grand Circumcision Festival
body: Murad III holds an extravagant 55-day festival for his son Prince Mehmed's circumcision, showcasing imperial wealth despite brewing economic inflation.

title: Battle of the Torches
body: A brutal night battle fought in a severe thunderstorm in the Caucasus results in an Ottoman victory over Safavid forces.

title: Crimean Succession Intervention
body: The Sublime Porte deposes Islam II Giray and installs a loyal Khan, solidifying tight Ottoman oversight over Crimean politics.

title: Conquest of Tabriz
body: Özdemiroğlu Osman Pasha captures Tabriz once again after fierce fighting during the eastern war.

title: Inflation and Currency Devaluation
body: Widespread economic inflation driven by American silver influxes and military costs triggers the first major Janissary coin riot in Istanbul.

title: Accession of Shah Abbas I
body: Shah Abbas I ascends the Safavid throne, initiating major military reforms that will soon reverse Ottoman eastern gains.

title: Koca Sinan Pasha's Vizierate
body: Experienced military commander Koca Sinan Pasha takes over the grand vizierate to stabilize internal military discipline.

title: Beylerbeyi Revolt
body: Janissaries mutiny in Istanbul over devalued pay, forcing the Sultan to dismiss ministers in the first major capital military revolt.

title: Treaty of Constantinople (1590)
body: The Ottoman Empire achieves its greatest territorial extent in the Caucasus, forcing Safavids to cede Tabriz, Georgia, and Azerbaijan.

title: Battle near Moscow
body: Crimean invasion under Ğazı II Giray meets fierce resistance; Russian victory halts Tatar expansion toward the capital.

title: Border Skirmishes in Croatia
body: Clashes between Ottoman Bosnian governors and Habsburg border commanders escalate along the Una River, paving the way for open war.

title: Long Turkish War Begins
body: A protracted conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Habsburg Monarchy begins, marked by stalemate and significant territorial shifts on the Hungarian frontier.

title: Fall of Győr (Raab) to Ottomans
body: Grand Vizier Koca Sinan Pasha captures the strategic fortress of Győr in Royal Hungary, shocking Christian Europe.

title: Accession of Mehmed III and Battle of Giurgiu
body: Murad III dies; Mehmed III ascends the throne, executing his 19 brothers, while Wallachian prince Michael the Brave inflicts heavy defeats on Ottoman forces at Giurgiu.

title: Egri Eyalet organized & Battle of Keresztes
body: Mehmed III personally leads the army to victory at the Battle of Keresztes and captures Eger, extending Ottoman administration into northern Hungary.

title: Stalemate in Hungary
body: Both Ottoman and Habsburg armies settle into mutual attrition around contested frontier fortresses like Vác and Esztergom.

title: Defense of Várad
body: Ottoman garrisons successfully hold major Hungarian border strongholds against Habsburg counter-sieges.

title: Celali Rebellions Begin
body: Disbanded soldiers, economic hardship, and rural dislocation spark widespread Celali peasant and bandit revolts across Anatolia.

title: Kanije Eyalet organized
body: Tiryaki Hasan Pasha successfully defends Nagykanizsa (Kanije) against a massive Habsburg siege, and it becomes the southwestern Ottoman Hungarian frontier center.

title: Siege of Kanije Repulsed
body: Habsburg forces under Archduke Ferdinand fail spectacularly to retake Kanije despite overwhelming numerical superiority.

title: Loss of Székesfehérvár
body: Habsburg forces temporarily capture Székesfehérvár (Alba Regia) from Ottoman control during autumn campaigning.

title: Accession of Ahmed I and Safavid War Resumption
body: Mehmed III dies; 13-year-old Ahmed I ascends the throne, while Shah Abbas I launches a major offensive to reclaim Caucasian territories lost in 1590.

title: Loss of Tabriz to Safavids
body: Shah Abbas recaptures Tabriz and pushes deep into Ottoman eastern provinces while imperial armies are tied down in Hungary.

title: Recapture of Esztergom & Celali Crisis
body: Grand Vizier Kuyucu Murad Pasha campaigns against Celali rebels in Anatolia while Ottoman forces retake Esztergom in Hungary.

title: Treaty of Zsitvatorok & Treaty of Vienna
body: The Long Turkish War ends with the Treaty of Zsitvatorok, ending annual Habsburg tribute and recognizing the Habsburg emperor as an equal to the Sultan, alongside the Treaty of Vienna.

title: Kuyucu Murad Pasha's Suppression of Celalis
body: Grand Vizier Kuyucu Murad Pasha launches a ruthless military campaign across Anatolia, executing tens of thousands of Celali rebels and restoring order.

title: Crushing of Remaining Celalis
body: Rebel leader Canbulatoğlu Ali Pasha is defeated near Damascus, effectively breaking the backbone of the devastating Celali uprisings.

title: Construction of the Blue Mosque
body: Construction begins on the Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) in Istanbul, symbolizing architectural renewal after years of crisis.

title: Campaign in Syria and Lebanon
body: Ottoman punitive expeditions re-establish strict central authority over autonomous Druze and regional lords in Mount Lebanon.

title: Stalemate on the Eastern Front
body: Low-intensity warfare continues in the Caucasus and western Iran against Shah Abbas's modernized forces.

title: Treaty of Nasuh Pasha
body: Borders are restored largely to those of 1555; the Ottomans lose all Caucasian conquests made under Murad III to Safavid Persia.

title: Revolt of Fakhr-al-Din II
body: Lebanese Druze leader Fakhr-al-Din II allies with Tuscany and rebels against Ottoman suzerainty, fleeing to Europe.

title: Execution of Nasuh Pasha
body: Grand Vizier Nasuh Pasha is executed over court corruption and treason allegations.

title: Border Tensions with Persia
body: Failure of Persia to pay agreed silk tributes sparks renewed friction along the eastern borderlands.

title: Death of Ahmed I and Accession of Mustafa I
body: Ahmed I dies prematurely; his mentally unstable brother Mustafa I is brought to the throne in a unique succession precedent.

title: Deposition of Mustafa I and Accession of Osman II
body: Mustafa I is deposed after a few months due to incompetence; young, ambitious Osman II is enthroned.

title: Treaty of Serav
body: Confirmed Safavid gains with modified silk trade and tribute arrangements, ending active eastern fighting for the moment.

title: Reforms of Osman II
body: Young Sultan Osman II attempts to centralize administration and curtail corrupt court and religious factions.

title: Outbreak of Polish-Ottoman War
body: Border clashes in Moldavia spark a direct war between the Ottoman Empire and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth over Cossack raids.

title: Battle of Khotyn
body: Osman II personally leads a massive expedition to Poland, but the siege of Khotyn bogs down against Cossack-Polish defenses, leading to a stalemate treaty.

title: Assassination of Osman II and Restoration of Mustafa I
body: Discontented Janissaries revolt against Osman II's proposed military reforms, dragging him to the Yedikule Fortress and assassinating him, restoring unstable Mustafa I.

title: Accession of Murad IV and Loss of Baghdad
body: Mustafa I is permanently deposed and confined; 11-year-old Murad IV ascends while Safavids seize Baghdad, plunging the empire into deep anarchy.

title: Abaza Pasha's Rebellion
body: Abaza Pasha launches a massive governor's rebellion in eastern Anatolia in revenge for Osman II's murder, backed by local tribes.

title: Failed Siege of Baghdad
body: Ottoman armies under Grand Vizier Gürcü Mehmed Pasha fail to recapture Baghdad from Shah Abbas after a grueling winter siege.

title: Cossack Raids on Istanbul Suburbs
body: Dnieper Cossacks launch audacious naval raids down the Black Sea, reaching the outer suburbs of Istanbul and burning towns.

title: Suppression of Abaza Pasha
body: Imperial forces defeat Abaza Pasha at Erzurum, ending his regional rebellion and restoring central control to eastern Anatolia.

title: Surrender of Abaza Pasha
body: Abaza Pasha surrenders to young Murad IV and is surprisingly pardoned, later appointed governor of Bosnia.

title: Preparation for Eastern Campaign
body: Murad IV begins taking personal control of government, brutally executing corrupt officials to restore absolute imperial authority.

title: Murad IV's First Eastern Campaign
body: Murad IV leads an army to retake Hamadan and besiege Baghdad, but severe weather forces an eventual withdrawal.

title: Janissary Mutinies in Istanbul
body: Janissaries revolt in Istanbul against Murad IV's strict disciplinary laws; the Sultan responds with swift, brutal executions.

title: Murad IV Assumes Absolute Power
body: Executing rebellious viziers and janissary ringleaders in the Hippodrome, 20-year-old Murad IV takes absolute personal control of the state.

title: Tobacco Ban and Istanbul Fires
body: Murad IV bans tobacco, coffee, and alcohol in Istanbul under pain of death following massive accidental city fires.

title: Polish-Ottoman War Avoided
body: Murad IV personally leads a successful campaign against Polish incursions in the Balkans, quickly signing a reaffirmation of peace.

title: Revan (Yerevan) Campaign
body: Murad IV leads a massive army into the Caucasus, capturing the strategic fortress of Revan (Yerevan) from the Safavids.

title: Safavid Counter-Offensive Repulsed
body: Persian armies retake Revan after Murad IV's departure, setting the stage for the definitive showdown over Mesopotamia.

title: Mobilization for Baghdad
body: Murad IV gathers the largest imperial army of his reign for a definitive campaign to recover Baghdad.

title: Recapture of Baghdad
body: Murad IV personally leads a brutal 39-day siege to successfully recapture Baghdad, ending 15 years of Persian occupation.

title: Treaty of Zuhab
body: Established the permanent modern Ottoman–Persian frontier; Iraq remained securely Ottoman while western Armenia and eastern Georgia went to Persia.

title: Death of Murad IV and Accession of Ibrahim I
body: Murad IV dies of cirrhosis at age 27; his eccentric, unstable brother Ibrahim I is pulled from confinement to take the throne.

title: Capture of Azov from Cossacks
body: Don Cossacks surrender the strategic fortress of Azov to Ottoman-Crimean forces after a prolonged siege.

title: Internal Court Intrigue
body: Sultan Ibrahim I leaves governance largely to mother Kösem Sultan and grand viziers while indulging in court eccentricities.

title: Financial Restructuring
body: Despite court chaos, capable viziers manage to stabilize imperial currency and tax collection temporarily.

title: Maltese Corsair Incident
body: Maltese corsairs capture an Ottoman ship carrying pilgrims and high officials to Mecca, sparking outrage and providing the pretext for the Cretan War.

title: Invasion of Crete (Cretan War)
body: Ottoman armies under Yusuf Pasha land in Crete, capturing Canea (Chania) in a brutal campaign against Venetian forces.

title: Siege of Rethymno
body: Ottoman forces capture Rethymno in Crete, steadily expanding control over the island while Venetian fleets blockade the Dardanelles.

title: Blockade of the Dardanelles
body: Venetian naval blockades severely disrupt grain and supply shipments to Istanbul, causing food shortages and capital panic.

title: Deposition and Execution of Ibrahim I & Crimean-Cossack Alliance
body: A violent coup led by Janissaries and religious scholars deposes and strangles Ibrahim I; 6-year-old Mehmed IV is enthroned, while Crimea allies with Bohdan Khmelnytsky.

title: Naval Battle of Phocaea
body: Venetian fleets inflict a heavy defeat on the Ottoman navy near Foça, maintaining the crippling blockade of the straits.

title: Venetian Dardanelles Blockade Peak
body: Venetian warships dominate the mouth of the Dardanelles, strangling Istanbul's maritime trade and fueling political instability.

title: Assassination of Kösem Sultan
body: Regent Kösem Sultan is murdered in a palace coup by Turhan Hatice (mother of Mehmed IV), ending the height of the Sultanate of Women.

title: Search for Strong Leadership
body: Rapid turnover of grand viziers fails to solve the crippling Venetian blockade and economic inflation.

title: Economic Strain and Inflation
body: Silver shortages and war costs in Crete paralyze provincial administration and tax yields.

title: First Battle of the Dardanelles
body: Ottoman naval forces break the Venetian blockade in a hard-fought battle, restoring vital supply lines to Istanbul.

title: Second Battle of the Dardanelles
body: Venetian Admiral Lazzaro Mocenigo defeats the Ottoman fleet outside the straits, though without fully restoring the blockade.

title: Appointment of Köprülü Mehmed Pasha
body: Desperate to save the empire, Turhan Hatice appoints 80-year-old Köprülü Mehmed Pasha as Grand Vizier with absolute dictatorial powers, launching the Köprülü Era.

title: Breaking the Venetian Blockade (Battle of the Dardanelles)
body: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha decisively smashes the Venetian blockade in a massive 4-day naval battle, reopening the Aegean and capturing Tenedos and Lemnos.

title: Suppression of Transylvanian Rebellion
body: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha leads a massive campaign into Transylvania to punish rebellious Prince George II Rákóczi and reassert Ottoman vassal control.

title: Purge of Disloyal Officials
body: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha ruthlessly executes corrupt governors and rebellious commanders across Anatolia, restoring iron discipline.

title: Varat Eyalet created & Great Istanbul Fire
body: Oradea (Varat) is captured and made the capital of a new Partium frontier province, while a massive fire devastates much of Istanbul.

title: Death of Köprülü Mehmed Pasha
body: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha dies, handing the grand vizierate smoothly to his equally capable son, Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha.

title: Preparations for Austro-Turkish War
body: Tensions rise along the Hungarian border as Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha prepares for a major showdown with the Habsburg Monarchy.

title: Uyvar Eyalet created (Nove Zamky Campaign)
body: Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha captures the formidable fortress of Uyvar (Nové Zámky) in Upper Hungary, creating a short-lived Ottoman province.

title: Battle of Saint Gotthard & Treaty of Vasvár
body: Ottoman forces are checked at the Battle of Saint Gotthard by Montecuccoli, but Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha secures favorable terms in the Treaty of Vasvár.

title: Rebuilding Palace and State Infrastructure
body: Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha focuses on administrative consolidation and rebuilding parts of Istanbul damaged by earlier fires.

title: Sabbatai Zevi Movement Suppressed
body: False messiah Sabbatai Zevi is arrested in Adrianople and forced to convert to Islam, ending a massive messianic Jewish movement.

title: Intensification of Cretan Siege
body: Grand Vizier Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha personally travels to Crete to take charge of the grueling, multi-year siege of Candia (Heraklion).

title: Stalemate at Candia
body: Engineering mines and artillery bombardments dominate the endless siege of Candia against stubborn Venetian and French volunteer defense.

title: Candia falls
body: Crete is absorbed after one of early modern Europe's longest sieges, concluding the 24-year Cretan War with total Ottoman victory.

title: Restructuring of Aegean Islands
body: Captured Cretan and Aegean ports are integrated into the Ottoman administrative and naval tax system.

title: Preparations for Polish War
body: The Sublime Porte prepares for an expedition against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth over control of Ukraine and Cossack territories.

title: Podolia annexed & Fall of Kamianets
body: The Ottoman Empire reaches its farthest northern European province, capturing the mighty fortress of Kamianets-Podilskyi.

title: Battle of Khotyn (Sobieski's Victory)
body: Polish commander Jan Sobieski crushes an Ottoman army at Khotyn, halting further expansion into Polish heartlands.

title: Russo-Ottoman Border Skirmishes
body: Tensions escalate with the Tsardom of Russia over control of Right-bank Ukraine and Cossack vassal allegiance.

title: Siege of Lviv
body: Ottoman and Tatar armies campaign through Ukraine, maintaining pressure on Polish borderlands.

title: Death of Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha
body: Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha dies; his brother-in-law Merzifonlu Kara Mustafa Pasha is appointed Grand Vizier.

title: First Siege of Chyhyryn
body: Ottoman defeat; Russian and Cossack forces successfully hold the fortress against Ottoman assault.

title: Chyhyryn Campaign
body: Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha personally leads an army to capture and utterly destroy Chyhyryn, turning back Russian advances.

title: Negotiations with Russia
body: Exhausted by Ukrainian border warfare, Ottoman and Russian diplomats begin talks to formalize a permanent frontier.

title: Border Stabilization in Ukraine
body: Minor skirmishes taper off along the Dnieper River line as both empires prepare for treaties.

title: Treaty of Bakhchisarai
body: Ottoman–Russian peace treaty signed; confirms Ottoman control of southern Right-bank Ukraine and Zaporozhian regions.

title: Upper Hungary & Imre Thököly Alliance
body: Imre Thököly receives Ottoman backing to establish a short-lived pro-Ottoman principality in Upper Hungary.

title: Second Siege of Vienna
body: Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha leads a massive army to besiege Vienna; John Sobieski's relief forces inflict a crushing defeat, beginning the strategic reversal of Ottoman power.

title: Formation of the Holy League
body: Pope Innocent VIII brokers the Holy League (Habsburgs, Poland, Venice, and later Russia) to systematically dismantle Ottoman European holdings.

title: Uyvar and Upper Hungary lost
body: Habsburg counteroffensives begin dismantling Ottoman Hungary, capturing key fortresses like Uyvar.

title: Fall of Buda
body: Habsburg forces capture Buda after a grueling 78-day siege, ending 145 years of Ottoman rule over the capital of Ottoman Hungary.

title: Battle of Mohács and Deposition of Mehmed IV
body: A catastrophic Ottoman defeat at the Second Battle of Mohács leads to military mutiny, the deposition of Sultan Mehmed IV, and the accession of Suleiman II.

title: Fall of Belgrade to Habsburgs
body: Imperial Habsburg forces under Maximilian II Emmanuel capture Belgrade, pushing Ottoman defenses deep into the central Balkans.

title: Habsburg Advance into Kosovo and Niš
body: Habsburg forces push deep into Ottoman territory, capturing Niš and entering Kosovo during the Great Turkish War.

title: Ottoman Counter-Offensive and Recapture of Belgrade
body: Grand Vizier Köprülü Fazıl Mustafa Pasha leads a brilliant counter-offensive, successfully recapturing Belgrade and stabilizing the northern frontier.

title: Battle of Slankamen
body: Heavy Ottoman defeat at the Battle of Slankamen where the capable Grand Vizier Köprülü Fazıl Mustafa Pasha is killed in action.

title: Siege of Petrovaradin
body: Ottoman forces attempt to check Habsburg expansion by fortifying and defending regional positions along the frontier.

title: Defense of Belgrade
body: Ottoman forces successfully hold Belgrade against a major Habsburg siege attempt, preserving a vital anchor on the Danube.

title: Capture of Giurgiu
body: Skirmishing and border warfare dominate the Danubian frontier with mixed engagements between Ottoman and Habsburg-Venetian coalitions.

title: Sultan Mustafa II's First Imperial Campaign
body: Sultan Mustafa II personally takes command of the field army, leading successful campaigns into Hungary and capturing Lipova.

title: Battle of Ulaş
body: Sultan Mustafa II defeats imperial forces in a hard-fought engagement in Hungary during his second personal campaign.

title: Disastrous Battle of Zenta
body: Prince Eugene of Savoy inflicts a crushing defeat on the Ottoman army led by Sultan Mustafa II at Zenta, leading to the loss of most of Hungary.

title: Prelude to Peace Negotiations
body: Exhausted by decades of continuous warfare and economic strain, the Ottoman Empire begins diplomatic overtures mediated by European powers.

title: Treaty of Karlowitz
body: The Ottoman Empire signs the Treaty of Karlowitz, ceding Hungary, Transylvania, and Podolia, marking the first major permanent loss of core territory in Ottoman history.

title: Treaty of Constantinople
body: Following the peace with Christian coalition states, the Ottoman Empire concludes a peace treaty with the Tsardom of Russia, ceding Azov.

title: Post-Karlowitz Administrative Restructuring
body: The Sublime Porte focuses on domestic reforms, military restructuring, and frontier fortification in the wake of the territorial losses of the Great Turkish War.
